descriptionChirho: Describes a literal bitter taste or an unpleasant, harsh quality of something (water, herbs, food, day).
Used in construct state to describe persons who are bitter/distressed in spirit or fierce in disposition (bitter of soul, bitter of heart).
Used adverbially to intensify an action, especially weeping or crying out (weep bitterly).
Used substantively to denote the abstract state of bitterness, anguish, or grief, often with prepositions indicating a condition or cause.
